revenueModel.knownConflict: $15 package is described as three officials in .planning/PROJECT.md but five drafts in MASTER_PLAN.md unit economics.

holes: May be a feature, not a venture-scale company.
Users may not convert at a paid checkout.
Official inboxes may reject or ignore AI-assisted correspondence.
Citation failures could be existential for trust and liability posture.
Human review volume may overwhelm the economics.
mitigations: Run a single-wedge beta before broad launch.
Measure official coverage and deliverability before scaling.
Require citation verification and human review for failures.
Track flagged queue minutes per day.
Treat public pages as optional and compliance-reviewed.
residualRisks: Market willingness to pay remains unknown.
Legal and reputation risk cannot be eliminated through automation alone.
Incumbents or general AI tools could copy the workflow.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Users will pay $5 to $25 for civic letter assistance.
Citation verification can prevent false legal references.
assumptionLedger.validation: Track citation pass rate and human-review fallback rate.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Official lookup providers can cover the first wedge.
Email delivery to officials will be reliable enough.
assumptionLedger.validation: Measure bounce, spam complaint, and accepted delivery rates by domain.

assumptionLedger.assumption: One operator can manage exception volume.
assumptionLedger.validation: Track daily queue depth and minutes per flagged submission.

goToMarket.wedge: Single metro or state wedge selected for official coverage and operator familiarity.
channels: Opt-in public campaign pages after compliance review
SEO only after the paid workflow works
